// why: Node runs this repository by STRIPPING types, which means it checks none of them. Three
signature changes in one afternoon — scoreCase, renderReading, checkQuote — surfaced as
test failures rather than as type errors, and would have surfaced as runtime errors in any
path a test does not cover. This file is what makes `tsc --noEmit` possible; nothing is
ever emitted from it, and the runtime remains node's own stripping.
`erasableSyntaxOnly` is the load-bearing setting: it refuses enums, parameter properties
and namespaces — the constructs node cannot strip — so the typechecker and the runtime
agree about what this repository is allowed to contain. Without it, tsc would happily pass
src/vendor/ is EXCLUDED here and checked by tsconfig.vendor.json instead, which relaxes
`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and nothing else. Vendored code is upstream's to write and ours
to re-copy, so holding it to a stricter setting than its own repository does would mean
patching 24 index accesses on every re-sync — a standing invitation to edit a copy that is
supposed to stay a copy. It is still typechecked, and still under `verbatimModuleSyntax`,
because that is the setting that catches the one class of error that actually stops the
vendored CLI from starting: a type imported without `import type` survives tsc's default
and does not survive node's stripping. `npm run typecheck` runs both files.
